html:
A small island in the Sierra Leone River where British traders kept a slave fort from about 1670, first for the Royal African Company and later for London merchant firms.

Tens of thousands of Africans were shipped from it, many to South Carolina and Georgia, where planters wanted people who knew how to grow rice. Their descendants include the Gullah people of the American coast, who keep ties to Sierra Leone. The trade from the island ended after Britain banned the slave trade in 1807, the year the colony at Freetown, a few miles downriver, became a Crown colony.
